members.title: China prefers to maintain relations with all political parties, whether in govt or in opposition: Liu Haixing
members.lead: Liu Haixing, minister of the International Department of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee, has said China prefers to maintain relations with all political parties, whether in govt or in opposition. "Where history illuminates the future, we see clearly that party-to-party exchanges play important roles in the development of our bilateral relations. We do not draw ideological lines, nor distinguish friends based on whether a party is in or out of government," he said in a written statement. Liu Haixing has made the remarks at the "Where History Illuminates the Future: China-Bangladesh “Political Parties Plus” Roundtable & Inauguration Ceremony of the Bangladesh-China Centre for Party and State Governance Studies." The Chinese leader said, "It gives me great pleasure to attend this roundtable. Listening to all our friends’ sharing just now has deeply touched me. Among you are witnesses to the establishment of China-Bangladesh diplomatic relations, participants in China-Bangladesh cooperation, and contributors to the friendship between our two countries." . "Through friendly exchanges with all major Bangladeshi political parties, we have added impetus to bilateral cooperation. Through in-depth exchanges and mutual learning, we have provided useful references for each other’s development," Liu Haixing added. He also said, "Through forging links and pooling efforts for people’s well-being, we have consolidated the popular support for China-Bangladesh friendship through “political party plus” channels. History has bestowed on us a precious friendship that spans generations." "Standing at a new historical starting point, we stand ready to work together with all sectors of society in Bangladesh to carry forward our friendship, foster consensus, deepen exchanges and mutual learning, and enhance people-to-people ties, so as to turn our traditional friendship into momentum for progress and let China-Bangladesh relations shine more brilliantly in the new era,…

members.title: Rizvi urges greater access for Bangladeshi products to Chinese market
members.lead: Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) Acting Secretary General Ruhul Kabir Rizvi urged greater access for Bangladeshi products to the Chinese market hoping that this would help reduce the existing trade deficit between the two countries. Noting that Bangladesh offered significant investment opportunities for Chinese investors in manufacturing, infrastructure, energy, information technology, agriculture and textiles, Rizvi said Chinese investors could capitalise on these opportunities. . Rizvi made the remarks at a roundtable titled 'Where History Illuminates the Future: China Bangladesh "Political Parties Plus",' organised by the Chinese Embassy in Dhaka. The Bangladesh-China Centre for Party and State Governance Studies was inaugurated afterwards. .China prefers to maintain relations with all political parties, whether in govt or in opposition: Liu Haixing. The senior BNP leader said the BNP was committed to pursuing an independent, balanced and forward-looking foreign policy based on Bangladesh's national interests. He emphasised the importance of further advancing the longstanding relationship with China, alongside increasing economic cooperation and investment. . Rizvi further said that the foundation of relations between Bangladesh and China had been laid during the tenure of Shaheed President Ziaur Rahman and had gained further momentum during the tenure of former Prime Minister Khaleda Zia. He emphasised advancing relations on the basis of long-term friendship, equality and mutual benefit. Rizvi said Bangladesh and China had longstanding relations based on friendship, mutual respect, trust and partnership. Communication and cooperation between the political parties and peoples of the two countries needed to be further strengthened. . At the event, Liu Haixing, minister of the International Department of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China (CPC), presented the keynote paper .
